title: Field Officer Bendigo

description: About This Role Enjoy a variety of field work and office-based work Ongoing, Full Time Opportunity in Bendigo Salary Range $72,189 - $79,753 plus superannuation Do you have great communication skills and want to be a role model to people hoping for a second chance? If you want to make time to help people get their lives back on track, read on. Who are we? Community Work and Partnerships We are responsible for the development of mutually beneficial partnerships with government agencies and non-government organisations so that individuals can undertake unpaid work as part of their community-based sentence imposed by the Courts of Victoria. Community work serves as a valuable way for individuals to pay back the community while also reconnecting and reintegrating into the community. We ensure individuals make genuine efforts to undergo rehabilitation, and we keep low risk individuals out of prison and help them contribute to the community. What does a Field Officer do? Your primary responsibility as a Field Officer will be to supervise a team of clients at community work sites and other community work programs. A field officer carries out many duties and functions, mainly the supervision of individuals completing community work tasks. Other responsibilities include performing site inspections, assess hazards, providing informed workplace health and safety advice, guidance and instruction; maintaining tools and equipment resister and ensuring repairs are undertaken. A day in the life of a Field Officer. . . Your shift starts at a Justice Service Centre location where you collect a bus/ trailer with equipment. You then drive to a site to collect a group of clients, where you will induct, instruct and transport them to a partner not-for-profit organisation in the community. Tasks for the day may involve graffiti removal, painting, litter collection, mowing and weeding. Your responsibility is to instruct the individuals to safely perform each task and monitor the work performed for the partner site before returning them to the drop off point and returning to your depot. We are looking for individuals with various backgrounds and experience. Some desirable skills include: You'll need to be able to communicate and demonstrate a range of tasks and ensure a safe environment for work teams. Have a strong understanding of Occupational Health and Safety practices and their practical application. Quickly build rapport in order to understand the motivations of others, identify issues and suggest courses of action appropriate to their needs. Have demonstrated ability to manage conflict and strong problem-solving skills. Model appropriate behaviours and attitudes to assist individuals to develop new skills and work practices. Carpentry or handyman skills Gardening landscaping or painting skills Field Officers carry out a mixture of field work and office-based work, so it's important that you are able to demonstrate computer skills and written communication skills. Transporting individuals is also a key part of the role and Field Officers will be required to drive a 12-seater bus with trailer. A full and current drivers' licence is essential for this position. Community Work operates seven days per week and this role will be required to work on weekends. Weekend availability is required. For More Information About The Role Please Contact Sarah Thompson â Manager, Community Work & Partnerships on 0407 427 396 or Sarah.Thompson@justice.vic.gov.au How To Apply Please click the Apply button at the bottom of this advertisement. Applications should include a resume uploaded in .doc, .docx, .pdf, .txt or .rtf formats. The Assessment Process Will Entail The Following Several questions in the application form upon submitting your resume A phone screen An interview Reference checks Security checks Health assessment â medical history and physical fitness components The successful candidate will be required to undergo pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, nationally coordinated criminal history checks (NCCHC), and misconduct screening. Dependant on the role, other checks may include VicRoads checks, drivers licence checks, medical checks, Working with Children Checks, and Declaration of Private Interests (for executive and responsible officer roles). If you require adjustments to the recruitment and selection process, or require an alternative format to any of the application material, please don't hesitate to get in touch with the contact person listed on this ad. Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply. Child Safe Statement Of Commitment The Department of Justice and Community Safety is committed to the safety and wellbeing of children and young people. We seek to prevent harm of any kind impacting children and young people and have zero tolerance for racism, child abuse and inequality. Children and young people's rights, relationships, identity, and culture must be recognised and respected, their voices heard, and their concerns acted upon. We aim to foster a culturally safe, child safe and child friendly environment for all children and young people we have contact with, deliver services to, or are impacted by our work. title: Wireperson
description: Description Trant Te-Tech design, custom build and install a wide range of high quality control panels, motor control centres (MCCs) and automation systems, offering conventional, intelligent and withdrawable systems with outstanding reliability and functionality. We are currently looking for a proven Wireperson to join our workshop based near Totton, Southampton. The Role The Wire Person is responsible for the accurate assembly and wiring of control panels, MCCs, and automation systems in accordance with electrical drawings, specifications, and applicable standards. The role plays a key part in ensuring assemblies meet quality, safety, and compliance requirements prior to inspection and testing. What Youll Be Doing Technical Responsibilities - Panel & MCC Wiring Carry out wiring of control panels, MCCs, and automation systems to approved schematics and wiring diagrams. Install and terminate power, control, and instrumentation cabling. Assemble and wire MCCs and control panels. Ensure correct segregation, routing and termination in line with design and compliance requirements. Technical Support & Collaboration Accurately interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, BOMs, and general arrangement drawings. Mark up drawings where required to reflect as-built changes. Follow work instructions and build documentation. Work collaboratively with fellow wire-people, testers, and supervisors to meet production targets. Support improvements in wiring practices, layout, and efficiency. Provide feedback to supervisors on build issues or potential improvements. SHE&Q and Compliance Carry out self-checks and peer checks prior to formal testing. Identify and report defects, non-conformances or drawing discrepancies. Work safely in accordance with company H&S procedures and UK legislation. Maintain a clean, tidy and organised working area. Use tools, equipment, and PPE correctly at all times. Key Interfaces: Internal Interfaces Workshop Supervisor. Production Manager. Test Engineer. Design & Engineering Teams. Automation Team. Stores / Logistic. Quality Team. External Interfaces Clients / Inspectors (as required) Suppliers (limited) Core Values Uphold and promote the Companys Core Values Care, Trust, Respect and Sustainability. What Were Looking For Essential NVQ Level 3 (or equivalent) in Electrical Installation, Panel Wiring, or Electrical Engineering. Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and GA drawings. Working knowledge of electrical safety practices and workshop H&S requirements. Familiarity with quality-controlled manufacturing processes. Proven experience wiring control panels, MCCs, or similar electrical assemblies. Experience terminating power, control, and instrumentation wiring. Experience working from schematics, wiring schedules, and BOMs. Experience completing work to high quality and safety standards in a workshop environment. Applicants must be legally authorised to work in the UK, as we are unable to sponsor work visas for this role. Desirable 18th Edition (BS 7671) qualification. Awareness or training relating to BS EN 61439-2:2021. Manufacturer or industry training on MCCs, switchgear andautomation systems. First Aid or IOSH Working Safely certification. Experience wiring MCCs and control panels. Experience with PLC I/O wiring, automation panels, and instrumentation. Experience supporting test and inspection activities, including rectification of faults. Experience working on custom-built, client-specific panel builds. Why Join Trant ? At Trant Engineering, we deliver complex, high-value engineering and construction projects across the UK. From process and water treatment to energy infrastructure upgrades, we play a key role in delivering and protecting critical national infrastructure shaping the systems that communities and industries rely on every day. Our teams design and deliver full EPC solutions, combining technical excellence with practical, hands-on delivery. We offer end-to-end capabilities from concept and design through to manufacturing, construction and commissioning utilising a continually evolving in-house expertise. This means youll work on projects that are varied, challenging and genuinely impactful. Our multi-disciplinary teams bring together specialists in civil, mechanical, electrical, process, instrumentation, and control & automation engineering, alongside our in-house manufacturing of control panels, MCCs, PLCs and SCADA systems. With over 1,000 people and a strong, growing pipeline of work, its an exciting time to join Trant. We are committed to helping our people succeed through our Career Development Association, providing structured support, mentoring and clear pathways to help you reach your full potential. Whether youre starting out or looking to take your next career step, Trant offers the chance to develop, progress and make a real difference. Our company benefits package includes: Competitive rates. 28 days holiday (including bank holidays). Options to buy additional holiday via salary sacrifice. Company pension scheme. Employee assistance program. Discretionary annual bonus. Join us and be part of something bigger. A high school diploma (or equivalent) and a valid trade license

title: English Teacher
description: Full-time, ongoing Commencing Term 1, 2027 Salary commensurate with years of Service Continuous professional development opportunities Generous staff benefits English at Pembroke is taught by a large, dynamic team across Years 7 to 12, spanning both SACE and the International Baccalaureate. Our Middle School curriculum has been recently redesigned around conceptual threads and a portfolio-based approach to assessment that prioritises the process of learning, not just its products. Our teachers enjoy considerable freedom in text selection, within a framework of high academic expectations, and our faculty culture is one of collegiality, intellectual curiosity and serious engagement with pedagogy. Our staff contribute to curriculum design, and are supported to grow as practitioners at every career stage. About the Role Successful applicants will teach across the secondary years, with allocations shaped by experience and strengths. Depending on the appointment, this may include Middle School classes, senior SACE English subjects, or IB Diploma Language A courses. Key Responsibilities include: Delivering engaging, rigorous and innovative English lessons that foster a love of learning Supporting students to develop strong literacy, analytical and communication skills Providing purposeful assessment and feedback that supports every students' growth Contributing to a positive and collaborative culture across the Middle and Senior Schools Actively participating in the life of the School through co-curricular and pastoral care contributions. About You You are an effective teacher first and foremost, with demonstrated impact on student learning and a command of your subject that lets you teach with both rigour and imagination. You will bring: Strong subject knowledge and a love of literature and language that students can feel Evidence-informed, responsive pedagogy and high expectations of every learner Capacity or willingness to teach across SACE and IB pathways (IB experience is valued but not required; training and support are provided) Strong communication with students, families and colleagues A collaborative disposition and a genuine interest in contributing to faculty and school life Applications at All Career Stages We welcome applications from experienced practitioners and from graduate and early-career teachers alike. Early-career appointees are supported through structured mentoring and induction as part of a faculty that takes professional growth seriously. Required for Employment (Prior to Commencement) Current Working with Children Check (South Australia) Current Plink RRHAN-EC training: Masterclass and Fundamentals, including Protective Practices First Aid and CPR Find Your Place At Pembroke At Pembroke, youâll be part of a warm and collaborative school community that values relationships, initiative, and a shared commitment to learning. Whether in the classroom, on the sporting field, or behind the scenes, every role contributes to shaping the rich and inclusive culture of the School. With opportunities for professional growth, a strong sense of belonging, and a genuine appreciation for staff, Pembroke is a place where your work is seen, valued, and celebrated. Read more in The Heart of Pembroke - Celebrating our Staff . Pembroke School is a co-educational, non-denominational, day and boarding School from Early Learning Centre to Year 12. Renowned for academic excellence and a broad, inclusive program, Pembroke offers the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE) and is also an International Baccalaureate World School, offering the IB Diploma Programme (IBDP) and Primary Years Programme (PYP). Pembroke is a vibrant and exciting School catering for a diverse community of students. With over 1,700 students, the School offers a broad-ranging curriculum and an outstanding choice of co-curricular opportunities. The School employs over 300 permanent and fixed-term staff, plus more than 150 casual employees. Pembroke seeks to engage outstanding, diverse and well-qualified staff to work in our welcoming and open School. All staff work together to provide an environment that facilitates each studentâs exploration of their potential, academic progress and personal welfare. Staff are encouraged to maintain a collaborative approach, a broad outlook within their respective field and a commitment to ongoing professional development and continuous improvement. Pembroke is a lively and fulfilling place to work. How to Apply Applications for this position close on Sunday, 6 September 2026, at 11:59 pm. You are required to upload a CV and a cover letter (maximum 2 pages) identifying your interest in applying and what you could bring to the role. Your application should be addressed to the Acting Principal, Mr Chris Zielinski. The School reserves the right to shortlist and interview candidates before the closing date. title: Course Director UX UI and AI
description: You've been designing long enough to have watched tools become essential and then disappear. You know which design skills are timeless and which ones expire.Â The human-centered design skills are where your heart is , and you know that AI will take over much of the tool-based design work soon. You see the fear around AI, and you understand where it comes from. But you also see the opportunities, and you want to show people how to work with AI in a way that benefits their lives, their users, and the world. You can name theÂ ten leading designers Â who should be teaching the worldâs best courses and Master Classes right now. You know what each of them does better than anyone else, and where their gaps are. Now you get the opportunity to decide what hundreds of thousands of designers learn next. The industry leaders whose expertise you'll be turning into courses and Master Classes includeÂ Don Norman and Vitaly Friedman , as well as Design Leads atÂ Netflix, LinkedIn, Meta, and Adobe . Don Norman also chairs our executive board. You'll be involved in the entire process of creating our courses and Master Classes, and you'll lead many of the decisions, so there are incredible opportunities for you toÂ take initiative, make meaningful contributions, and grow . Forget political struggles or long, pointless debates. Youâll be in a team with minimal distance between idea and action, where decisions are made ultra-fast. Join the Global Leader in Online Design and AI Education IxDF is the world's largest online design and AI education platform, with over 1,150,000 enrollments since 2002. We hold the trust of industry giants like Adobe, NASA, and IBM, who rely on our courses to train their teams. Prestigious universities, including MIT and the University of Cambridge, integrate our material into their curricula. Help us take online education to new heights Â andÂ make a meaningful impact on humankind . At IxDF, weâre not just a company but a movement dedicated to making high-quality design and AI education accessible to everyone, everywhere. We've pioneered online design education since 2002. We have over 1,150,000 enrollments and 1,583 company members, with more than 40 courses, 160 Master Classes, and thousands of open-source design resources, created by our team in collaboration with 240 industry leaders. With learners from over 100 countries, your work will empower people worldwide. We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on: Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI : lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers.Â This is the role described here. Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI : lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there. Our Course Writers and Editors : lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the userâs perspective. We're a flexible team, and you'll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why. You, the Course Director , decide what belongs in our curriculum and who should teach it. You reach out to the worldâs leading experts, plan the courses with them, and shoot courses with them. When an Education Designer brings you a course outline, you're the one who says what's missing, what doesn't belong, and how to optimize the learning outcome so designers can succeed today. You'll work closely with ourÂ Co-Founder , yourÂ Team Lead , our otherÂ Course Directors , and theÂ Education Designers , and you'll plan and create courses alongside them. Our Course Writers and Editors take the finished material the last mile: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team. Your Role at IxDF Be a core part of our Editorial Team . You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design. You'll research what already exists in a topic area, so that what we build is genuinely unique. You'll look atÂ where design and AI are heading, what designers needÂ that nobody has taught well yet, andÂ what we should retireÂ because the field has already moved on. Find the people who should teach it. Â You decide a topic is worth a course, you work out who should teach it and why, you write the email, and you get the yes. Then you plan the content with the industry leader and agree what the course must leave a learner able to do. Decide what each expert should teach. Â The best designers know a great deal, and a course that tries to capture all of it becomes an information dump. You develop a point of view on what a designer genuinely needs from them, and you hold the course to it. You'll decide which skills our courses teach , both to people entering design and to experienced designers leveling up. Our goal is to help designers thrive in the age of AI and work responsibly, so their users can thrive too. Ensure our course participants finish each course with a solid portfolio project they can show a hiring manager. Help us decide what AI should do for our course participants . Personalized learning paths, constructive AI feedback on portfolio work, practice environments where people run real design tasks and get feedback. You'll also help us improve the user flows on our own platform, so that learning at IxDF is as well designed as what we teach. You'll work on this with our founders, designers, and dev team. Make an impact as you pressure-test the coursesÂ our Education Designers plan. An Education Designer sends you a course outline, and you read it against everything you know about the field and about how people learn design, then give constructive feedback on what's missing, what doesn't belong, and where the structure can be improved. Â You know the limits of your own expertise , and you research your way past them before you weigh in. You'll also plan, structure, and create courses yourself, alongside them. You're one of the people Â whose judgment the rest of the team leans on. Â You show our Education Designers what ten or twenty years in the field taught you to look for. In return, our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, and our other Course Directors give constructive feedback on the courses you lead. You'll work in aÂ diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment Â where you'll grow personally and professionally. Act as guardian of our quality bar . When a course goes out under our name, it has to be better than anything else available on the topic. On the courses and Master Classes you lead or review, you're the one who spots what's not good enough yet and works with the team to fix it. About the role

For more than 60 years, Complex has been known for delivering award winning construction projects across the built environment.


Our skillful execution of quality projects is an expression of our personal and professional commitment to connecting and enhancing communities.


We are looking for a Lead Estimator, this role will provide support and technical advice to our estimating team, deliver accurate, competitive, and well-documented cost estimates for civil & construction projects, while also providing oversight and tender coordination to the estimating team.


The Lead Estimator is a critical role that remains hands-on in the preparation of tenders while contributing to pricing strategy, subcontractor engagement, and achieving tendering milestones.


Key responsibilities

  • Prepare accurate and competitive cost estimates, budgets, and scopes of work for civil construction tenders
  • Review tender documentation (drawings, specifications, RFTs, contracts) to confirm scope, risks, and opportunities
  • Conduct and/or coordinate site inspections to assess conditions and identify construction risks
  • Perform and review quantity take-offs using Benchmark, Revu, and Excel
  • Prepare detailed cost build-ups, subcontractor comparisons, and pricing reconciliations
  • Analyse historical project data to support pricing accuracy and continuous improvement
  • Promote consistent estimating methodologies, tools, and documentation standards
  • Maintain effective working relationships with key subcontractors and suppliers

About you

  • Minimum 5 years' experience in commercial construction / civil infrastructure estimating
  • Demonstrated experience preparing and leading complex civil tenders
  • Strong understanding of civil, building and construction methodologies, contract review and risk identification, and cost planning and pricing strategy
  • Proven ability to mentor and support junior and mid-level estimators
  • High-level competency in Benchmark, Bluebeam Revu, Microsoft Excel, and Microsoft Project (Intermediate level)
  • Ability to manage multiple tenders and competing deadlines
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Well-developed interpersonal, negotiation, and organisational skills


If this sounds like you please APPLY reach out to Ebony Ison, ebony.ison@complexco.com.au


This role is also advertised on SEEK Lead Estimator Job in Canberra ACT - SEEK
